newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit lower in light trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit lower in light trade.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open marginally lower Wednesday as forecasters called for moderating temperatures in the East and Midwest over the holiday weekend, market sources said.
August over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.095 to $2.11 after settling to the downside Tuesday at $2.11 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, August last traded 0.7 cent lower at $2.103.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were talked about one cent lower at $2.13-2.16 per mmBtu.

Technically, traders said August support was at $2.08, and then at $2.05. Resistance was seen at $2.15 and then along the trendline at $2.27. Further selling was likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.
However, the absence of many traders will likely keep the contract range-bound into early next week, market sources said. NYMEX will close at 1300 EDT Thursday ahead of the Independence Day holiday.

In Wednesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices were unchanged to a penny lower in the low-teens. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly around $2.03-2.05. New York city gate gas was quoted modestly lower in the low-to-mid $2.40s.
Supporting cash over the last few days have been the above-normal temperatures across most of the U.S., which are forecast to linger into Thursday.

However, cooler air is expected to arrive by Friday throughout the East and Midwest, according to Weather Services Corp, which will likely put some significant downward pressure on an already soft market.
Separately, injection estimates for today's weekly AGA stock report range from 75-105 bcf, versus a 93 bcf build a year ago.
